slides.title: A Role Often Misunderstood
bullets: Prior lessons covered IIS, observational studies, registries, evidence plans
This lesson consolidates the MSL's global research function
It's one of the most frequently misread parts of the role
Misread both inside and outside the organization

slides.title: Three Things the MSL Doesn't Do
bullets: Does not design studies
Does not statistically analyze data
Does not decide what research gets funded
Those belong to clinical research, biostatistics, and medical strategy

slides.title: The Connection Node
bullets: MSL links field scientific reality to the org's evidence machinery
Four concrete capabilities define this, per MSL Society frameworks
None of them involve designing or deciding the science itself

slides.title: Listening, Then Guiding Process
bullets: Active scientific listening captures hypotheses and unresolved problems
Systematic capture is the first layer of MSL research value
Process orientation helps investigators formalize a study idea correctly
Without ever influencing the proposal's scientific content

slides.title: Facilitating and Feeding Strategy
bullets: Facilitates the link between investigators and internal teams
Clinical research, HEOR, and regulatory affairs, with proper documentation
Feeds evidence planning with aggregated field intelligence
Arguably the most strategic of the four capabilities

slides.title: MSL and CRA, Complementary Roles
bullets: CRA ensures operational execution and regulatory compliance
MSL brings scientific context and a trusted investigator relationship
MSL connects that research to broader medical priorities
The two roles are complementary, never interchangeable

slides.title: Precision Protects Credibility
bullets: Knowing these limits lets an MSL contribute without overstepping
Avoids drifting into commercial influence or scientific design
Precision here preserves the integrity of the whole function

takeaway.title: The MSL's research role is connection, not design: listening, guiding process, facilitating relationships, and feeding strategy
bullets: Study design, data analysis, and funding decisions sit elsewhere
Four capabilities define the role, none of them scientific control
The MSL-CRA comparison shows complementary, not overlapping, value
